newsitem.title: CANADA: British Columbia cogeneration plant moves forward.
newsitem.headline: British Columbia cogeneration plant moves forward.

text.p: Westcoast Energy Inc and Fletcher Challenge Canada Ltd are expected to begin building a C$225 million gas-fired cogeneration project in British Columbia next February, the provincial government said Wednesday.
Construction is expected to start when environmental permits are received. The plant should go into operation by December 1999, the Ministry of Employment and Investment said.
The plant would be built adjacent to a Fletcher Challenge pulp and paper mill at Elk Falls on Vancouver Island.
The two companies, which proposed the joint venture project last year, have moved a step forward by agreeing with British Columbia Hydro on a plan for the utility to buy power from the plant.
"This agreement takes us one step closer to the construction of Canada's largest independently owned gas-fired cogeneration plant," Westcoast official Graham Wilson said.
The Island Cogeneration Project will generate 240 megawatts of power and an average of 1,921 gigawatt hours of electricity a year, or roughly enough to supply 200,000 households.
The arrangement with BC Hydro makes power available for sale to the utility for about 20 years.
